description_paragraphs: The crew of the spaceship Nostrom responds to a distress signal, leading to brief contact with a small unknown species. Thankfully, Ellen Ripley is on board to help everyone follow protocol. The crew listens to her and keeps the potentially infected crewmemberoff the ship until JUST KIDDING! THEY IGNORE HER AND TOTALLY LET THE GUY BACK ON BOARD AND GO TO SPACE LIKE "IT'S FINE." And one bad but somewhat understandable decision leads to a whole mess of unexpected complications. Director Ridley Scott focused on the visual experience, bringing in famed artist H.R. giger to design the title creature. the result is a true classic. Sigourney Weaver stars as Ellen Ripley, one of sci-fi's most iconic heroes.

description_paragraphs: Do you love movies and want to find others who can talk endlessly about them? Come join Cinemancy! Each month, a new movie is carefully selected, then we gather to discuss themes, characters, plot, and symbolism. Hosted by Isabella Price. July's movie: Crouching Tiger Hidden Dragon Western audiences at large finally embraced the beauty and thrills of martial arts films thanks to Ang Lee's acclaimed film. Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon tells the tale of two warriors tracking a stolen sword whose worth goes beyond that of a simple weapon. Also in the mix are a wealthy teen noble who desires more than a life of prim and proper princess, and a young outlaw who never expected love to be part of his story. Nominated for ten Oscars and winning four, Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon became the first foreign language blockbuster in the United States for a good reason. It's a film worthy of the big screen, and one you'll want to talk about with fellow film lovers the moment it's over.

raw.calendar_title: CrossFaded Cinema: The Wizard of Oz
description_paragraphs: CrossFaded Cinema is a film series curated by DJ NicFit, providing a unique live remix of classic and cult films. For his first show at Central Cinema, he's bringing the legendary theatrical mash-up of Pink Floyd and the Emerald City. Young Dorothy finds herself in a magical world where she makes friends with a lion, a scarecrow and a tin man as they make their way along the yellow brick road to talk with the Wizard and ask for the things they miss most in their lives. The Wicked Witch of the West is the only thing that could stop them. DJ NicFit mixes live on stage as we follow the Yellow Brick Road.

While the good folx at The Grand Illusion Cinema locate a new home, they’ll host their monthly Hundreds of Beavers screenings at Central Cinema.
In this 19th century, supernatural winter epic, a drunken applejack salesman must go from zero to hero and become North America’s greatest fur trapper by defeating hundreds of beavers.

description_paragraphs: When the seaside community of Amity finds itself under attack by a dangerous great white shark, the town's chief of police, a young marine biologist, and a grizzled shark hunter embark on a desperate quest to kill the beast before it strikes again. That's the official description. But here's how it should read: When the seaside community of Amity finds itself under attack by a dangerous great white shark, they don't do anything. The Mayor is like, "Oh well. Let's keep tourist season going." Meanwhile, the shark just does what sharks do, and you can't blame it for that. Except the mayor does blame the shark and is all, "I don't know how to kill a shark. you three do it." Winner of three Academy Awards including one for John Williams' iconic score.

Why, build a theme park on a remote island, of course. But before he opens it to the public, he brings some dinosaur experts plus Jeff Goldblum to his island to make sure bringing people to the park is a good idea. Spoiler: It's not. Spielberg's classic dino adventure is a perfect summer flick, with another iconic score from John Williams. Feel free to sing along.

raw.calendar_title: Baron Von Terror presents: Night of the Creeps
description_paragraphs: The good news is your dates are here. The bad news is they're dead. The best news is Baron Von Terror's bringing you a real 80s gem for July. In 1959, an alien experiment crashes to earth and infects a fraternity member. They freeze the body, but in the modern day, two geeks pledging a fraternity accidentally thaw the corpse, which proceeds to infect the campus with parasites that transform their hosts into killer zombies. Writer/Director Fred Dekker deliberately put in every B-movie trope he could think of with this very funny sci-fi creep flick. Practical make-up and icky effects fill the big screen, with the Baron on hand to help you survive the Night of the Creeps!

description_paragraphs: Two households, both alike in dignity In fair Verona, where we lay our scene, From ancient grudge break to new mutiny, Where civil blood makes civil hands unclean. So begins the tale of Romeo + Juliet (it's actually a full sonnett with MAJOR spoilers). Where director Baz Luhrman takes it from there is unlike any Shakespearean adaptaion before or since. While drawing only from the original text, the film goes beyond simply setting the film in modern times, making the story feel fresh in a way that holds up 30 years later. Of course, being a Baz Luhrman film, it also comes with gorgeous production values and a top notch soundtrack. The cast is stacked, with Claire Daines in particular earning various accolades at the time for her take on Juliet.

raw.calendar_title: Seattle Scare Society Presents: The Return of the Living Dead
description_paragraphs: Seattle, we know better than to play with a barrel of toxic gas containing a corpse, yes? Because not everybody knows this. To help us all learn, Seattle Scare Society brings you Return of the Living Dead.

This bona fide 80s classic is a favorite among horror fans for its blend of comedy, thrills, and practical make-up effects. This movie is so iconic, it literally changed the scope of zombie lore in popular culture and how we perceive their diet.
Seattle Scare Society starts the show 30 minutes before the movie with trivia and prizes, so come early and prepare your delicious brains for a night of big screen fun.

raw.calendar_title: The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou
description_paragraphs: Is this a Father's Day movie? Many people have complicated relationships with their dads, so sure, we'll go with it. Renowned oceanographer Steve Zissou has sworn vengeance upon the rare shark that devoured a member of his crew. In addition to his regular team, he is joined on his boat by Ned, a man who believes Zissou to be his father, and Jane, a journalist pregnant by a married man. They travel the sea, all too often running into pirates and, perhaps more traumatically, various figures from Zissou's past, including his estranged wife, Eleanor.

description_paragraphs: Loosely based on Romeo and Juliet, Valley Girl is a tale of a preppy and a punk finding love in the 1980s. Julie, a trendy teen from the Valley, meets Randy, a young city punk. The unlikely duo quickly find themselves smitten, even though their friends don't understand the mismatched pair. Will they be able to stick together despite their differences? And what will happen when Randy shows up to Julie's prom? Director Martha Coolidge (Real Genius) crafts a fine 80s teen rom-com, with charming lead performances from Nic Cage and Demorah Foreman.
